title: Split primes and the Elekes-Rónyai problem
summary: There exist an absolute constant $c>0$ and arbitrarily large finite sets $A\subset \mathbb{R}$ with $$\left| \left\{x+y+(x-y)^2:\ x, y \in A\right\}\right| \le|A|^{2-c}.$$ Since $x+y+(x-y)^2 \in \mathbb{R}[x,y]$ is a polynomial which is neither additive nor multiplicative, this provides a counterexample for the Elekes-Rónyai problem. The proof combines two amplifications of the same local congruence defect: horizontal amplification over squarefree products of rational primes, and vertical amplification through bounded root-discriminant towers in which those primes split completely.
